records.region: Southern Victoria Island, Nunavut: the northern approaches to the western Ferguson Lake basin and its Ekalluk River outlet into Wellington Bay.
records.candidate_name_role: Bounded supported lower lake-to-bay outlet identity only; whole selected system remains material pending because inland through-links are unestablished.
records.material_pending_reason: Original parts5–15 leave the western lake shore and cross the adjacent land peninsula before reaching the actual southern outlet arm. Both the historical map and independent photography show the connected lake passage farther east/south, while land, relief and small separate wet hollows occupy the selected intervening route. The necessary selected through-link is not established at ordinary connected lake/valley/wetland scale. The long first part also has a bounded unconfirmed western feeder link between its opening lake setting and the clearly visible southward receiving corridor; neighboring lakes and thin channels alone do not prove that chosen transfer.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The mapped lower Ekalluk River outlet between the historically named Ferguson Lake and Wellington Bay. This supported receiving-river name is not extended unconditionally to the entire selected northern feeder/lake/peninsula composite.
records.completion_scope: The bounded pass accounts for all19 original parts and77 stored positions of stage3 mainstem FID2362. Receiving-valley, lake and terminal geography are supported in the stated components; the parts5–15 peninsula transfer and a bounded first-part feeder link remain unestablished. The primary result is source_material_pending, not a completed null-name scope hold. There is no new source-access failure and no automatic application.
records.supported_name_scope: The mapped lower Ekalluk River outlet between the historically named Ferguson Lake and Wellington Bay. This supported receiving-river name is not extended unconditionally to the entire selected northern feeder/lake/peninsula composite.

scope_limits: The west-side peninsula transfer in parts5–15 lacks the necessary connected geographic support.
The long first part’s western feeder transfer is not independently established; the southward receiving valley itself is located.
The known lake’s connected outlet arm follows a different, more easterly/southerly route than the selected peninsula crossing.
The lower Ekalluk receiving-river name is supported, but cannot by itself complete the composite selection.
No current preferred lake name, formal naming boundary, surveyed source or exact contemporary wet thread is asserted.

The lower Ekalluk name and historical Ferguson Lake/Wellington Bay association are supported. Naming that lower receiver does not resolve the selected peninsula crossing or assign names to every northern feeder and pool.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
